messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: P99 latency for generation-api (hosted) exceeding 800ms for last 5m. Error budget at 72%. Link: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/1819777777

jamie-sre: ack — paging oncall now. I'm jumping in, pulling traces.

natalie-eng: seeing a huge uptick in streaming connection churn + CPU on router pods in us-west-2. Non-streaming (poll) traffic not spiking as much.

jamie-sre: good catch. hypothesis: streaming SSE fanout + KV cache overhead is causing request storm and head-of-line blocking.

omar-prodops: current traffic shaping rules: 100 rps per customer, short-burst=200. We can tighten to 40 rps and reduce burst to 60 while we stabilize. Want me to apply?

jamie-sre: yes, do it. Also can we flip streaming feature toggle to false for hosted tier for 10m as a mitigation? This will force clients to fallback to long-poll/resumable which should cut connection overhead.

carla-ml: FYI, disabling streaming will affect some latency-sensitive apps but should reduce per-connection GPU context churn. We'll monitor decoding times.

omar-prodops: applying rate-limit change now: `kubectl exec -n infra ratectl --update --bucket-size=60 --max-rps=40 --target=hosted`. Rolling through edge nodes.

omar-prodops: rate-limits rolled to 60s buckets, max-rps=40. Propagation ~30s.

jamie-sre: initiating toggle: `curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.internal/api/v1/flags/disable_streaming -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' -d '{"scope":"hosted","enabled":false,"reason":"incident-1819777777-mitigation"}'`

jamie-sre: toggle submitted, got 202. Pushing change via feature-service, will verify via /health/flags endpoint.

tess-support: posting brief to support channel: "We're seeing elevated gen latencies; we've temporarily disabled streaming on hosted API and tightened rate limits while we stabilize. Customers may see degraded interactivity. We'll post updates. — Ops"

rachael-custsuc: pinging top-10 customers on the affected tier with a templated note + mitigation ETA.

natalie-eng: dashboards show immediate drop in TCP connection counts on frontends. CPU on router pods dropping ~35% in last 2m.

jamie-sre: good signal. P99 now ~420ms (was 920ms). Error budget improving.

carla-ml: running quick smoke against model-serving: streaming disabled -> tokens still generated fine via poll path. No model OOM observed.

omar-prodops: I also bumped tenant quotas for free tier to limit simultaneous sessions: `redis-cli MULTI \nHSET tenant:free:limits sessions 2 \nEXEC` — applied.

jamie-sre: next steps: keep rate limits + streaming off for another 15m, watch for regression. If stable, do a staged re-enable (10% -> 30% -> 100%) with canary.

natalie-eng: can we add a temporary fallback route on the router to send heavy-hitter customers to dedicated capacity (if they have it) to reduce noise?

omar-prodops: we have a mapped list. I'll whitelist top 5 enterprise tenants to dedicated lanes. Doing now.

tess-support: queued a customer advisory draft for legal/comms review. Will not mention internal flags, just "temporary interactivity changes" and ETA.

jamie-sre: status update in 10m. tagging oncall handoff @natalie-eng for next shift if needed.

-- 30 minutes later --

incident-bot: UPDATE: p99 latency stable at 380ms for 10m window. No new alerts.

natalie-eng: system stable under tightened limits. Recommend staged re-enable: flip 10% streaming on (canary) and monitor p99 for 5m.

jamie-sre: agreed. Omar, can you roll 10% flag? Use `gradual=true, pct=10` param.

omar-prodops: submitted canary: `POST /flags/disable_streaming {"scope":"hosted","gradual":true,"pct":90}` -> effectively 10% enabled.

omar-prodops: canary active.

natalie-eng: monitoring: no regression at 10%, p99 steady 410ms. CPU holds.

jamie-sre: escalate to 30% after 5m of green.

omar-prodops: moving to 70% disable (30% enabled). Propagating.

natalie-eng: 30% enabled -> slight increase p99 to 440ms but within SLO. Continue to 100% in staged steps once corporate customers confirm no issues.

rachael-custsuc: enterprise accounts on the whitelist report no added issues; some have turned on poll-mode client handling already.

-- 2 hours after root --

jamie-sre: incident summary for postmortem: root cause likely streaming connection overhead + KV cache eviction storm from a small set of heavy-hitter customers triggering router CPU pressure. Mitigation: temporary disable streaming on hosted, tighten rate limits, whitelist enterprise to dedicated lanes.

jamie-sre: action items: (1) postmortem writeup (owner: jamie-sre), (2) better heavy-hitter detection + automated routing (owner: natalie-eng), (3) review default streaming quotas and make more aggressive soft-limits (owner: omar-prodops), (4) customer communications follow-up (owner: rachael-custsuc).

tess-support: closing incident channel in 1h if metrics stay green.

jamie-sre: incident resolved -> will mark as "mitigated" and keep monitoring. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
